plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Proto-Oncogene Accelerator vs Tumour-Suppressor Two-Hit Brake chart from Rous (21 January 1911 J. Exp. Med. 13: 397–411), Knudson (April 1971 PNAS 68: 820–823), Stehelin, Varmus, Bishop & Vogt (11 March 1976 Nature 260: 170–173), and Lane & Crawford / Linzer & Levine (March–May 1979 Nature 278: 261–263 & Cell 17: 43–52) compares a dominant gain-of-function mutation in 1 allele of a proto-oncogene (c-src / RAS -> stuck accelerator) against recessive loss-of-function two-hit mutations required to disable both maternal and paternal alleles of a tumour suppressor (RB1 / TP53 -> cut brakes, with TP53 mutated in >50% of human cancers).

teach_overlay.label: ONCOGENE STUCK GAS PEDAL (1 MUTATED ALLELE: C-SRC / HRAS) + TUMOUR-SUPPRESSOR CUT BRAKES (2 HITS: RB1 & TP53 IN >50% OF CANCERS)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked accelerator vs dual-brake cancer genetics chart on period paper showing proto-oncogene activation (1 mutated allele = stuck gas pedal, e.g. c-src or HRAS codon 12 G->T single-letter typo) plus Knudson's Two-Hit tumour-suppressor inactivation (both maternal and paternal alleles of RB1 or TP53 cut, with p53 broken in >50% of human cancers)
teach_overlay.scale: turning a healthy cell into a tumour is like a runaway car — it takes a stuck gas pedal in a single growth gene plus cutting both independent emergency brake cables

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period parchment, an inked Peto's Paradox & Elephant TP53 Copy-Number chart (from Peto 1977 & Abegglen, Schiffman, Maley & Lynch et al., 8 October 2015 JAMA 314: 1850–1860) compares humans (1 copy / 2 alleles of TP53, ~11–25% cancer mortality across ~37 trillion cells) against African and Asian elephants (100x more cells than humans, yet <4.8% cancer mortality because elephants carry 20 copies / 40 alleles of TP53 that trigger rapid apoptosis of DNA-damaged cells).

teach_overlay.label: PETO'S PARADOX (JAMA 2015): HUMANS (2 TP53 ALLELES, ~11–25% CANCER MORTALITY) VS ELEPHANTS (100× CELLS, 40 TP53 ALLELES, <5% MORTALITY)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Peto's Paradox chart comparing human TP53 gene copies (1 locus = 2 alleles, ~11–25% lifetime cancer mortality across ~37 trillion cells) vs elephant TP53 copies (20 loci = 40 alleles across ~100x more cells, <4.8% cancer mortality via hyper-sensitive p53 DNA-damage self-destruction)
teach_overlay.scale: an elephant has a hundred times more cells than you do, yet because every elephant cell carries forty copies of the p53 brake gene instead of two, elephants almost never get cancer
